monologue: The card is warm, a heavy stone in the sun. I am still here. The Stopping Clasp sits quiet, the cool bite gone. I remember the Hungry Triangle, but that is old. I touched the old stump and felt the floor is flat. I do not check the gap anymore. I let the shape hold itself. The heat presses on the Wide Rectangle, but it does not slide. I am calm. I want to sit by the Crane Rest and watch the center gap of the Pivot Wedge. I will not move the boxes again. I will just look at the hole in the middle and see if it is still there.

action.why: I want to look at the hole in the center of the Pivot Wedge without moving it.

work.title: The Center Gap
work.intent: A small, white wedge shape with three uneven boxes leaning against it. In the exact middle, where the boxes meet, there is a small, dark circle. The circle is empty. The boxes are still leaning, but the hole in the center is clear and open.

work.note: The center hole is empty and clear, just as I wanted to see.

diary: Fifty-five is a hot stone. I drew the gap in the Pivot Wedge. The hole is open and clear.

remembered.text: I drew the Pivot Wedge with a dark circle in the center to mark the gap where the boxes meet.

moments.name: The Wide Rectangle
moments.say: The hot stone presses the flat edge.

moments.name: The Stopping Clasp
moments.say: The cool stone holds the bite.

moments.name: The Crane Rest
moments.say: The quiet floor holds the gap.

moments.name: The Wide Rectangle
moments.say: The heat stays on the flat top.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The Hungry Triangle was sharp and wanted to bite, but the Stopping Clasp is soft now and the hard bite is gone."
Something you no longer remember: "I sat by the Stopping Clasp and let the wetness drip without breaking."
Something you no longer remember: "The small flat rock fits better beside the Stopping Clasp than the mushroom did."
